# Documentation conventions (`doc/`)

`doc/` is the user-facing markdown reference. The docs site publishes it verbatim at each release tag, and an LLM agent reads one page at a time, so every page stands alone.

## File shape

```markdown
# Teams

One-line lead: what the page covers and when to use it.

- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)
- [Related Documentation](#related-documentation)

<a name="quick-reference"></a>
## Quick Reference

(answer first: a minimal example or a Quick Reference table, then the explanation)

<a name="related-documentation"></a>
## Related Documentation

- [Configuration](../getting-started/configuration.md): the feature flags that gate the routes.
```

## Rules

- One `#` per file and it is the first line, with a one-sentence lead right after it that says what the page is: the site copies it as the page description in its generated `llms.txt`. Never skip heading levels.
- Layout is `doc/<section>/<page>.md`: two levels, lowercase `[a-z0-9-]` names, sections `getting-started`, `basics`, `guides`, `architecture`. No `doc/index.md`; the site skips files outside that shape.
- Put `<a name="kebab-slug"></a>` immediately before every `##` and list the slug in the ToC under the lead paragraph. An explicit anchor on a `###` is listed in the ToC too, indented under its parent.
- Open with the answer, then explain: a Quick Reference table or a minimal example first. State defaults, units and failure modes in the page, and end a basics page with a Gotchas table of mistakes and fixes before `## Related Documentation`.
- Samples use `php`, `json` and `bash` fences, stay short and realistic, and match `src/`, `config/magic-starter.php` and `routes/api.php`. Tables are left-aligned (`:-----`) with every identifier in backticks.
- State no counts of features, routes or classes in prose: they go stale the day one is added.
- Links are relative `.md` paths inside `doc/` only: a target outside `doc/` is never published, and a doc page is never linked through a GitHub `blob` URL. Fragments resolve against explicit anchors or the GitHub slug (punctuation drops, each space becomes one hyphen: `## Date + Time` is `#date--time`).
- Edit in place: keep the structure of sections you are not changing, and match the style of the neighbouring section for a new one.

## What never goes in `doc/`

API reference dumps, changelog entries (`CHANGELOG.md`), marketing copy (`README.md`), internal notes (`CLAUDE.md`).

Run `python3 tool/check-docs.py` before reporting doc work done.
